posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Damn.  Should have taken Tweedledee up on his offer to repeat history.  That 'spirit' being just 'mostly dead' isn't gonna cut it...having to blow up all these alien tinker-toys twice is going to be a pain in my superhumanly perfect ass.  (I figure that the Visionary is probably at least a little bit of a deviant, considering her costume, and she was put through a "super soldier" project, so she's gotta be in spectacular shape.)

The time-traveling psychic frowned.  I guess I'm going to have to settle for doing whatever I can.  The pillars on either side of the room were positively pulsating with what the science of her future home had come to refer to as 'pseudothaumaturgic power currents' (known on the streets as 'ley lines', and greatly misunderstood), and for her brain to tap into them and augment its own power was as easy as reaching up and getting something off an overhead shelf.  Channeling the surplus mojo into an act of mental multitasking which would normally have made her black out from cognitive overload, she unleashed a wave of barely-visible mental mojo which had two simultaneous effects (as far as any casual onlooker could tell).  It telekinetically shattered the glorified gazing ball which the deceiver was using to focus the room's feng shui or whatever, and it also implanted a telepathic demand in his mind to pick up the dozens of sharp-edged pieces (preferably with his teeth, but she doubted that part of the command would stick), and try to reassemble him with nothing to use for glue.

She no sooner finished sending the theta-wave pulse with these instructions than she was struck with a precognitive flash - curses!  He was actually going to be able to do it, with remarkable speed and efficiency no less.  Something about the energy channels implanted in the walls - apparently, for atlantean super-science, refusing shards of jagged glass into a geometrically perfect was a routine household chore.  Oh well, at least it would keep him busy for a few seconds while they regrouped.  And hopefully he wouldn't notice how she'd quietly erased his ability to perceive the invisible, largely innocuous creature which he'd been planning on using to maintain his stolen artifacts.  Without instructions from him, the 'spirit' (actually some Atlantean servitor, probably a standing-wave hologram generated by nannites) would just drift around the room aimlessly, no more dangerous than the puff of fetid air for which a layman would mistake it.

The Visionary

HP:  19

Hand:  Mass Levitation, Suggestion, Psychic Maelstrom, Twist the Ether, Mind Spike

In Play:  Foresight, Mental Divergence

Trash:  Brain Burn

Deck: 30x ?, Telekinetic Cocoon, Mind Spike

-------------------------

Start of Turn:  Pillars of Hercules puts out the Gauntlet of Perdition.  Visionary does not skip her turn.

Play Cards:  Mind Spike for 1 net damage to the Orb [X], then Suggestion - the Relic Spirit goes to the bottom of Apostate's deck and the Orb goes on top.

Use Powers:  Foresight.  Reveal Foresight, Wrest the Mind and Mind Spike; put Foresight on the bottom.  Then Enlighten to draw one net card, a Decoy Projection, and discard Mass Levitation.  (I was going to resolve Foresight first and then see whether anyone had an Ongoing for me to return with Mental Divergence, but I decided I was more interested in digging for my Precognitions, in the hopes of avoiding a Profane Summons which will undo all my deck-stacking.  Normally I bemoan the ease with which Visionary can entirely gimp a villain's plays, but in this case he's really making me work for it, and when I pick a strategy I tend to stick with it rather stubbornly.)

Draw Cards:  Mental Divergence, Cerebral Hemorrhage

End of Turn:

-------------------------

HP:  19

Hand:  Psychic Maelstrom, Twist the Ether, Wrest the Mind, Mind Spike, Decoy Projection, Mental Divergence, Cerebral Hemorrhage

In Play:   Foresight, Mental Divergence

Trash:  Brain Burn, Mass Levitation, Suggestion, Mind Spike

Deck:  24x ?, Telekinetic Cocoon, Mind Spike, Foresight

"Tachyon, darling, I don't want to tell you what to do - well, okay, truthfully I do really want to do that, but you'd think it was terribly impolite and so I'm not actually doing it.  But I would like to judiciously recommend that you busy yourself with finding the 'off' switch for this ancient arcane mechanism, before our adversary is able to harness its full potential.  I confess I have enjoyed utilizing the surplus psionic energies which it radiates, and so I can't fault you if you choose to do the same, but it would be an unnecessary risk in a confrontation which I am working dutifully to keep under control."

posts.cooked: Um, why not play the Suggestion before Mind Spike?  That way, we don't get nailed with the Orb/Runes combo and the Orb still dies.

posts.cooked: If the Relic Spirit isn't put to the bottom of the deck, its death brings back the destroyed orb.  And if Suggestion has only 1 target, that target goes to the top per the wording on the card, so it means a new Relic Spirit would arrive and thus need to be killed.  This way's not ideal, but it's better.  Orb/Runes is a serious problem, but it's not one we can easily avoid.
